correctness.rationale: For all n>=2 and 0<=a<1, direct strict-order half-weight tests give a fixed rank-to-median map characterized by q. In the stationary-core case this yields fixed leaders and e^(-t) exterior relaxation; in the even central-pair case a two-coordinate system decays with e^(-2t) and all other ranks solve forced linear equations. Each proposed formula stays ordered for finite t, so it solves the original ODE branch globally; the nonexpansive nearest-own median map permits continuous extension to arbitrary initial ties and uniqueness. All boundaries use <= median inequalities. The embedded exact-rational checker separately passed 1,755 profiles and 56,160 derivative/median comparisons. These tests support but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The homogeneous complete social network is a canonical, motivated benchmark for weighted-median compromise. This exact classification maps every initial condition to a precise limiting profile, gives the full transient, distinguishes the parity-dependent universal-consensus thresholds, and quantifies the sharp sequence of polarization bifurcations as self-influence increases. Neither existence of equilibria nor generic convergence alone answers which opinions remain or the two competing decay scales; the combined exact result is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary unmotivated slice.
